scope: four project main sessions in the frozen archive; textual structured records and metadata
method: Parsed every JSONL record and checked record types, message roles, channels, phases, nested field names, session metadata and manifest hashes.
Scanned parsed string values for credential patterns, internal prompt markers and authentication/configuration file content patterns; filename mentions alone were not treated as credential leakage.
Checked tool call/return identifiers in each session and counted embedded PNG data URI occurrences.
Reviewed README.md and HANDOFF.md: both accurately state that only this migration package is published and the latest local H implementation and material reorganization are not included.
boundaries: This is a pattern-based audit, not a guarantee that every form of private or sensitive meaning can be identified automatically.

The archive intentionally retains user-visible conversations, tool outputs and historical local paths. Private semantics, personal details and organization-specific information are not comprehensively classified by these checks.
Embedded PNG bytes were counted but were not subjected to OCR or a full visual privacy review; the count is data URI occurrences, not a uniqueness claim.
Authentication/configuration checks detect recognized content structures; the result does not claim universal detection of every possible file format.
The audit covers exactly archive_sha256 above. It does not audit a later re-export or arbitrary future exporter output.

visual_review.review: Reviewed 3 contact sheets of all 66 decodable unique images; they show course diagrams, plots, demo renders and course UI captures. No credential screen observed. This was not OCR.
